He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook Seawolves]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. ==Early life== Gueye was born in [[Staten Island, New York]], to Senegalese parents who played basketball.{{cite web|first=Craig|last=Meyer|title=How Pitt's Mouhamadou Gueye took a narrow, fortuitous path to becoming an ACC starter|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2022/01/21/pitt-panthers-basketball-mouhamadou-gueye-jeff-capel-stony-brook-monroe-college-staten-island/stories/202201210088|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=October 9, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Herrmann|title=Reaching New Heights: 'They said I would be tall. They didn’t know I was going to be 6-9 tall.'|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2020/1/23/mens-basketball-reaching-new-heights-they-said-i-would-be-tall-they-didn-t-know-i-was-going-to-be-6-9-tall|work=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=January 23, 2020|access-date=October 9, 2022}} His father, Ababacar, moved to Staten Island from [[Senegal]] in 1987 with $100 and saved money from a job in construction so that his wife, Souwadou, could join him a few years later. Gueye shared a passion for basketball with his father who would watch cassette tape games of their hometown [[New York Knicks]] and Ababacar's favourite player [[Michael Jordan]]. He played with friends at local parks and recreation centres in addition to his father paying for him to work with a trainer. ==High school career== Gueye attended [[Curtis High School]] in Staten Island and started as a {{height|ft=5|in=9}} [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] before he grew {{convert|10|in|cm}} over four years. He did not play on the school's basketball team during his junior or senior seasons due to disciplinary measures arising from his [[truancy]]. Gueye was invited to play for a local [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, iWork Basketball, during his senior year. A teammate uploaded a highlight reel of Gueye's play to [[YouTube]] which was noticed by an assistant coach at [[Monroe College]].{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Peak|title=Pitt's newest transfer looking to make his name|url=https://pittsburgh.rivals.com/news/pitt-s-newest-transfer-looking-to-make-his-name?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAADHzk6Z_3kyboJgK7xJ-cZFMcon3COiGwaRssNFlsxRqnmh8WicyeNBB3A9mOhdhl33H8JJHAXB1NCQ-oxQMfyx545r7L6J4ttIMaVg-v37TbEoZ7Whan7zUyTFKRTJyHgv-MtNFQLAQOlwfvPMBwNbttY9Ot7NgE_Np9QhASL14|work=Panther-lair|date=June 1, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2022}} Gueye was invited for a workout on campus and was offered a spot on the roster when the coaches saw his ball-handling and passing abilities. ==College career== Gueye debuted at Monroe, in the [[NJCAA]], during the 2016–17 season when he averaged 2.1 points and 3.6 rebounds per game. He sat out the 2017–18 season because of academic issues. Gueye's playing ability increased when he returned for his sophomore season in 2018–19 and attracted the interest of several colleges. Gueye made the jump to the [[NCAA Division I]] level as he transferred to the [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook Seawolves]] ahead of the [[2019–20 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|2019–20]] season, where he learned how to play effectively within a system by knowing when to set screens, take shots and make passes. On December 8, 2019, Gueye made two plays against defending champions [[2019–20 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] that both made the [[SportsCenter]] Top 10.{{cite web|title=Reaching New Heights: 'They said I would be tall. They didn’t know I was going to be 6-9 tall.'|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2020/1/23/mens-basketball-reaching-new-heights-they-said-i-would-be-tall-they-didn-t-know-i-was-going-to-be-6-9-tall|website=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=January 23, 2020|access-date=February 11, 2024}} Gueye made the SportsCenter Top 10 again after a January 8, 2020 [[slam dunk]] on [[Anthony Lamb (basketball)|Anthony Lamb]] of [[2019–20 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]].{{cite web|title=STONY BROOK MEN’S BASKETBALL: 2019-20 GAME NOTES|url=https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/sidearm.nextgen.sites/stonybrook.sidearmsports.com/documents/2020/2/20/27_Vermont.pdf}} He appeared in 33 games and made eight starts. In his second season with the Seawolves, he was named [[America East Conference|America East]] Defensive Player of the Year, averaging 3.1 blocks per game. He was also named to the All-Conference Third Team. Gueye ranked in the top ten nationally in blocks, and had eight against [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]] on February 7, 2021, one shy of the program record.{{cite web|title=SBU Sports: Men’s hoops edged by UMBC as Seawolves begin crucial stretch {{!}} TBR News Media|url=https://tbrnewsmedia.com/sbu-sports-mens-hoops-edged-by-umbc-as-seawolves-begin-crucial-stretch/|website=TBRNewsMedia.com|date=February 10, 2021|access-date=February 11, 2024}}{{cite web|title=BLOCK PARTY! Mo Gueye Named America East Defense Player of Year|url=https://stonybrookathletics.com/news/2021/2/25/mens-basketball-block-party-mo-gueye-named-america-east-defense-player-of-year.aspx|work=Stony Brook University Athletics|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 11, 2024}} He had 129 blocks in two seasons at Stony Brook, the second most in the program's Division I history.{{cite web|title=PSU, Pitt both add size|url=https://www.altoonamirror.com/sports/local-sports/2021/06/psu-pitt-both-add-size/|website=AltoonaMirror.com|access-date=February 11, 2024}} With an extra year of eligibility owing to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Gueye transferred to the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] for his final season of college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Pitt Lands 2021 America East Defensive Player of the Year Mouhamadou Gueye|url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2021/6/8/mens-basketball-pitt-lands-2021-american-east-defensive-player-of-the-year-mouhamadou-gueye.aspx|work=University of Pittsburgh Athletics|date=June 8, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Saxon|title=Gueye’s emergence gives Pitt men’s basketball a ‘different look’|url=https://pittnews.com/article/170440/top-stories/gueyes-emergence-gives-pitt-mens-basketball-a-different-look/|work=The Pitt News|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=October 9, 2022}} He averaged 9.8 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game during the 2021–22 season with the Panthers.{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks Fill Out Training Camp Roster With Five Signees|url=https://www.mavs.com/camp-signees-2/|website=Mavs.com|date=September 21, 2022|access-date=October 9, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Texas Legends (2022–2023)=== On September 21, 2022, Gueye signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was waived by the Mavericks on October 12, 2022.{{cite web|title=Mavs Waive Tyler Hall, DJ Stewart, Marcus Bingham, Mouhamadou Gueye|url=https://hoopswire.com/mavs-waive-tyler-hall-dj-stewart-marcus-bingham-mouhamadou-gueye/|website=HoopsWire.com|access-date=October 13, 2022}} On October 23, 2022, Gueye was listed on the training camp roster of the Mavericks' [[NBA G League]] affiliate team, [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|title=Legends Draft Two, Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-draft-two-finalize-training-camp-roster/n-5892719|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 30, 2022}} On November 3, 2022, Gueye was named to the opening night roster for the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|title=Legends Announce 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895504|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} He averaged 8.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.9 blocks per game in 29 games played. ===Toronto Raptors / Raptors 905 (2023–2024)=== Gueye joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=RAPTORS ANNOUNCE NBA SUMMER LEAGUE 2023 ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-announce-nba-summer-league-2023-roster|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} and on July 21, 2023, the Legends traded his G League rights to the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|title=Legends Acquire 2024 1st Round Pick|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-acquire-2024-1st-round-pick/n-5992116|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=July 21, 2023|access-date=July 22, 2023}} On August 1, he signed a contract with the Raptors,{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN TEMPLE, GUEYE AND OBANOR|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-temple-gueye-and-obanor|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2023|access-date=August 1, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE DOWTIN JR, GUEYE AND WINSLOW|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-dowtin-jr-gueye-and-winslow|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2022}} Ten days later, he joined the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS 905 FINALIZES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-finalizes-training-camp-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 11, 2023}} On December 1, he sustained a neck injury during the game against the Maine Celtics.{{cite web|title=Raptors 905 lose another player to injury as Mouhamadou Gueye leaves on stretcher|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/raptors-905-lose-another-player-to-injury-as-mouhamadou-gueye-leaves-on-stretcher/article_9241328a-4e15-514c-b2c9-6555d05eb9c6.html|website=TheStar.com|date=December 1, 2023|access-date=December 1, 2023}} Gueye was the leading candidate for a [[two-way contract]] with Toronto at the time but the injury ruled him out; the team instead signed [[Jontay Porter]].{{cite web|first=Blake|last=Murphy|title=Raptors Notebook: Frequent slow starts hard to overcome|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-notebook-frequent-slow-starts-hard-to-overcome/|website=SportsNet.ca|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=April 21, 2024}} On February 10, 2024, Gueye signed a 10-day contract with Toronto{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN WINSLOW AND GUEYE TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-winslow-and-gueye-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}} and two days later, he made his NBA debut on February 12 against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], recording two points, three rebounds and two blocks in six minutes.{{cite web|first=Stephen|last=Thompson|title=Former Pitt F Mouhamadou Gueye Makes NBA Debut|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/basketball/former-pitt-panthers-mouhamadou-gueye-makes-nba-debut|website=SI.com|date=February 13, 2024|access-date=February 14, 2024}} On February 20, he returned to Raptors 905{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Raptors 905 Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 21, 2024}} and on March 4, he signed a two-way contract with Toronto.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN GUEYE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-gueye-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 4, 2024}} Gueye appeared in 11 games for Toronto and averaged 2.4 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Raptors' Mouhamadou Gueye: Ruled out for season finale|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-mouhamadou-gueye-ruled-out-for-season-finale/|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 13, 2024|access-date=April 21, 2024}} On June 25, 2024, the Raptors waived Gueye.{{cite web|title=Raptors waive forward Mouhamadou Gueye, open up two-way spot|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-waive-forward-mouhamadou-gueye-open-up-two-way-spot/|website=SportsNet.ca|date=June 25, 2024|access-date=June 25, 2024}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2024–2025)=== After joining the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|first=Juan Carlos|last=Blanco|title=2024 California Classic Summer League: Mouhamadou Gueye, [[Washington Wizards]] on October 13, 2024.{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=Official: The Washington Wizards have signed F Mouhamadou Gueye to an Exhibit 10 contract.|number=1845573999247397357|user=WizPRStats|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} However, he was waived six days later{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=The Washington 2024}} and on October 28, he joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} ===Windy City / Chicago Bulls (2025–2026)=== On September 10, 2025, Gueye signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web|title=Bulls continue to fortify forward depth with under-the-radar free agent signing|url=https://pippenainteasy.com/bulls-continue-fortify-forward-depth-with-under-radar-free-agent-signing|access-date=October 30, 2025|website=pippenainteasy.com|language=en}} He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on October 13.{{Cite web|title=Bulls cut ties with 6-foot-9 former Raptors forward|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/bulls-cut-ties-6-foot-195903470.html|access-date=October 30, 2025|website=ca.sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} Gueye played for the [[Windy City Bulls]] for the [[2025–26 NBA G League season]], averaging 15.9 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. On April 9, 2026, Gueye signed a contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web|title=Chicago Bulls sign Mouhamadou Gueye|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-mouhamadou-gueye|access-date=April 9, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} He scored 11 points in the season finale against the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |date=2026-04-13 |title=Bulls' Mouhamadou Gueye: Strong line in finale |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-mouhamadou-gueye-strong-line-in-finale/ |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} === Valencia Basket (2026–present) === the Chicago Bulls, but was waived shortly after.{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Naz Reid, Multiple Draft Picks From Minnesota For Lamelo Ball And Josh Green |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-naz-reid-multiple-draft-picks-from-minnesota-for-lamelo-ball-and-josh-green |access-date=July 10, 2026 |publisher=[[Charlotte
